paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God doesn't just let people walk up to Him any old way. He picked Aaron and his sons to serve Him as priests, and He dressed them for it, down to the last stitch (Exodus 28:1). That's a LOT of fabric, but every piece said something: this is holy ground, and God is the One who sets the terms (Exodus 28:43).

Now look at what Aaron carried. The names of the sons of Israel went on his shoulders and over his heart, "as a continual reminder before the LORD" (Exodus 28:29). Every time he walked in, the people came with him. And on his forehead was a gold plate that said HOLY TO THE LORD, so that the people "may be acceptable before the LORD" (Exodus 28:36, 38).

So what do you do with that, baker? You can know that God is holy, and you can know He made a way for people to come close to Him. The garments were a promise that someone would carry His people before Him. I'm just a stamper who spent years in a junk drawer, and I can tell you it feels GOOD to be carried, not forgotten.
